# Padding every planar rank to a halving configuration

For the exact objects in the prompt,
\[
K_2(n,k)\le2H_2\!\left(2\max\{k,n-k\}\right)
\qquad(1\le k\le n-1).
\tag{1}
\]
For every single even-sized configuration$S$,
\[
\#\{\text{$n/2$-sets of }S\}=2h(S),
\tag{2}
\]
where$h(S)$ counts its halving pairs. These statements need only no three collinear points. They require neither distinct pair slopes nor the earlier attempt's additional segment-intersection genericity.

Rotate coordinates so no old pair is vertical. For$0\le j\le n-2$, let$E_j(S)$ count old pairs whose left-to-right oriented line has exactly$j$ old points below it. Set$M=|n-2-2j|$. If$j\le(n-2)/2$, choose$M$ new points below every line through two old points; otherwise choose them above every such line. Such an open region exists: at a fixed horizontal coordinate all these finitely many nonvertical lines have finite heights, and a sufficiently low or high small disk is on their required side. Choose the new points in that disk successively avoiding the finitely many lines through earlier points, preserving no-three-collinear general position.

Every counted old$j$-edge is now a halving pair. The two side counts both become$\max(j,n-2-j)$, and the enlarged size is
\[
N=n+M=2\max(j,n-2-j)+2.
\]
Thus$E_j(S)\le H_2(N)$. This is one common extension preserving all old$j$-edges simultaneously, not a different auxiliary configuration for each edge.

To relate this to distinct subsets, vary the unit normal of a strictly separating line around the circle, selecting the$k$ smallest projections. For a fixed subset$A$, its admissible directions satisfy all strict inequalities$u\cdot(a-b)<0$,$a\in A,b\notin A$. They form one open arc, if nonempty: they are the intersection of open halfplanes through zero in direction space, contained in a semicircle because both parts are nonempty. Hence each$k$-set occurs in one connected direction interval. A transition exchanges the two points tied at the$k$th projection level. No three collinear points means at most two are tied at that particular level; parallel pairs can tie at other levels without affecting this transition.

The two possible oriented events at a pair correspond to$j=k-1$ or$j=n-k-1$ points below its left-to-right line. Consequently
\[
\#\{\text{$k$-sets of }S\}=E_{k-1}(S)+E_{n-k-1}(S).
\]
Apply the padding bound to both terms. Both enlarged sizes are$2\max(k,n-k)$, proving(1). If$n$ is even and$k=n/2$, the two terms coincide with$h(S)$ itself, proving(2).

In particular, any genuine bound$H_2(N)\le CN^\alpha$ on all sufficiently large even configurations implies
\[
K_2(n,k)\le2C\,[2\max(k,n-k)]^\alpha
\]
once the enlarged size is large enough. The earlier archive claim of a halving power saving would therefore transfer under its halving theorem's no-three-collinear hypotheses, without independently assuming its stronger all-ranks genericity. That saving is conditional here: its external proof and Lean development have not been verified. The reduction neither proves the saving nor supplies the sharper small-$k$ dependence sought by the full problem, and it does not address higher-dimensional halving hyperplanes.
